          record-transport: job-output
          pull-request: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
          wait-for-verification: 'false'
          provider-key: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
          typesafe-key: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }}

  # Runs in this same workflow run only when the receipt-only job above found the receipt unusable. This is
  # the only job that holds the provider secrets for a PR that carries a receipt marker, and it never reads the
  # receipt (ignore-receipt) or any value derived from it: it receives just the PR number and the frozen engine.
  assess-hosted:
    if: needs.assess-intent.outputs.hosted == 'true'
    needs: [assess-intent, resolve-clouseau]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 70
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
    outputs:
      assessment: ${{ steps.assess.outputs.assessment }}
      review-record: ${{ steps.assess.outputs.review-record }}
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      # Never load the controller or its configuration from the PR.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Review the change through the installed CI AI reviewer, ignoring the receipt
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        id: assess
        with:
          operation: assess
          ignore-receipt: 'true'
          record-transport: job-output
          pull-request: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number }}
          wait-for-verification: 'false'
          provider-key: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
          typesafe-key: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }}

  approve-and-merge:
    name: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) || (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))) && 'approve-and-merge' || 'metadata-only-approval' }}
    needs: [assess-intent, assess-hosted, resolve-clouseau]
    # Always resolve the job name; only trusted, ready PR events run its steps.
    # A failed assessment must still fail the required native approval check.
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    concurrency:
      group: pr-approval-${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number || github.run_id }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - name: Require a completed assessment
        if: >-
          ((github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) ||
          (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))) &&
          (needs.assess-intent.result != 'success' || contains(fromJSON('["failure","cancelled"]'), needs.assess-hosted.result))
        run: exit 1
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: *review-event
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        if: *review-event
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - if: *review-event
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: gate
          record-transport: job-output
          # Exactly one acceptance record per head: the hosted review's when it ran, otherwise the receipt-only job's.
          review-record: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.review-record || needs.assess-intent.outputs.review-record }}
          pull-request: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number }}
          native-gate: 'true'
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}

  apply-repair:
    needs: [assess-intent, assess-hosted, approve-and-merge, resolve-clouseau]
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      needs.assess-intent.result == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), needs.assess-hosted.result) &&
      needs.approve-and-merge.result == 'failure' &&
      fromJSON(needs.assess-hosted.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment).repair_digest != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: read
      actions: read
    concurrency:
      group: pr-approval-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: repair
          record-transport: job-output
          review-record: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.review-record || needs.assess-intent.outputs.review-record }}
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}
          repair-token: ${{ secrets.CLOUSEAU_REPAIR_TOKEN }}

  finalize-merge:
    needs: [assess-intent, assess-hosted, approve-and-merge, resolve-clouseau]
    if: *review-event
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      actions: write
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: finalize
          pull-request: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number }}
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}

  request-reassessment:
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/approve-intent ')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request != '' && !inputs.check_author)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      actions: write
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: request-reassessment
          pull-request: ${{ inputs.pull_request }}

  check-author:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.check_author
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - name: Verify independent repair author without writing
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.CLOUSEAU_REPAIR_TOKEN }}
          script: |
            const {data: user} = await github.rest.users.getAuthenticated();
            const {data: repository} = await github.rest.repos.get(context.repo);
            if (user.login === 'github-actions[bot]' || !repository.permissions?.push) {
              throw new Error('Repair requires an independent author with Contents write access');
            }
            core.info(`Independent repair author ${user.login} can access ${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}. No write or deployment was made.`);

claims.title: feat(ci): follow protected main with the resolve bootstrap
claims.description: Owner decision: the hosted CI bootstrap gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve must always follow the latest protected main, not a pinned commit. The engine itself is resolved from protected main at run time and runs with the repository's secrets, so a commit pin on the small bootstrap adds little protection and creates stale pins. New installs, examples/consumer-ci.yml, customer-facing docs (README, quickstart, initial installation, automatic CI upgrades, change acceptance, local review) and Clouseau's own self-hosting workflows reference gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main. Validators (engineContext seeding in src/central-version.cjs, the shared workflow contract test/automatic-upgrade-contract.mjs and the workflow tests) accept @main and an existing full 40-hex commit, and reject every other moving reference (tag, other branch, fork, other action path) via the new resolverReference. Exact 100% line and branch coverage, review-compatibility statement bumped compatible because behavior for every previously accepted input is unchanged. Do not touch any consumer repo.

report.summary: The change switches the Clouseau bootstrap reference to resolve@main, still accepts an existing full 40-hex commit, and rejects tags, other branches, forks and other action paths in the contract test and the new resolverReference helper. It also updates engine-seed selection, docs, the example workflow, the self-hosting workflows and the compatibility statement. Local verification passed: exact 100% line and branch coverage, the archive check and 47 workflow tests. I found no causal defect. The one security-relevant effect is that the bootstrap action now follows a mutable ref, which the stated owner decision and the unchanged frozen engine SHA/digest binding accept. The exact-head owner confirmation for workflow control changes belongs to CI.

name: Clouseau base reconciliation
# Merges made by the bot with GITHUB_TOKEN raise no push event, so a push-triggered reconciliation never
# runs on the unattended path. This workflow follows the completion of the review workflow ("Clouseau CI")
# for a pull request and, when that pull request has been merged, finds every other approved pull request
# that the merge left behind. It must be a separate file: a workflow is never started by its own completion.
# Nothing is approved, merged or re-armed here. No update token is configured: a stale approved pull request
# receives a clouseau-needs-branch-update notice. Only trusted main and the frozen engine are ever checked out;
# pull request code is never checked out or executed.
run-name: Reconcile base (${{ github.event_name }}${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch && format(' {0}', github.event.workflow_run.head_branch) || '' }})
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Clouseau CI"]
    types: [completed]
  # Covers an auto-merge that completes after the review run has ended, and recovers a missed event.
  schedule:
    - cron: '11,41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  resolve-clouseau:
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request_target'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      sha: ${{ steps.engine.outputs.sha }}
      digest: ${{ steps.engine.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - id: engine
        uses: gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main

  reconcile-base:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request_target')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10

There is no application-specific deployment infrastructure in Clouseau.

## Operations

Automatic CI integrations reference the small `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main`
bootstrap, so it always follows the latest protected main (the engine is resolved from protected
main at run time with the repository's secrets, so a commit pin on the bootstrap adds little and
only goes stale). It selects protected Clouseau main,
freezes its SHA and computes its digest. Every engine job checks out that SHA
and invokes the local action with the same trusted outputs. Normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest update; existing full-commit references keep working. See [automatic CI upgrades](docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
for source authorization, failure behavior and exact local-receipt compatibility.
Legacy fixed installations may still use `gaulatti/clouseau@FULL_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA`;
upgrading those installations requires a reviewed PR. See `examples/colombo.json`
for the version 2 policy configuration.

| Operation | Inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verify-engine` | Trusted run SHA/digest in `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA` and `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST` | Verify the frozen source and record its exact identity |
| `test` | none | Run Clouseau's Node regression suite |
| `coverage` | Accepted-base v2 `coverage-config`, or legacy `coverage-report` + `source-directory` with optional `coverage-format` | Require exact, nonempty 100% native application line and branch coverage; the two input forms are mutually exclusive. A repository can opt in to [changed-line coverage](docs/changed-line-coverage.md) with `coverage.mode` in its protected config plus `coverage-base-ref` and `coverage-baseline` |
| `await-verification` | `config`, `pull-request` for non-PR events | Wait for the exact-head PR verification run without deadlocking a single-slot runner pool: ends cleanly with `verified=false` when verification has not started within `verification_queue_grace_seconds` (default 900), to be reassessed when the verification run completes |
| `assess` | `config`, optional `pull-request`, `provider-key`, optional `ignore-receipt: 'true'` (never read the PR's receipt; for the hosted fallback after an unusable receipt) | Authenticate local quality evidence independently of technical status, or wait for verification before CI AI assessment |
| `verify-local` | `config`, eligible published signed receipt | Validate local evidence and independent CI with zero AI calls; missing or invalid evidence holds |
| `gate` | `config`, `assessment`, optional `pull-request` | Validate protection, arm auto-merge, request owner review, or approve a verified revision |
| `repair` | v2 `config`, `assessment`, this run's record artifacts, independent `repair-token` | Validate and reserve one bounded correction, then push a new internal PR revision requiring fresh CI/review |
| `evaluate-acceptance` | `provider-key`, `typesafe-key` | Execute six fixed qualification fixtures, investigate with real models, compare DeepSeek and Jev grading plus whole-review cost; retain evidence without GitHub writes |
| `evaluate-review` | `provider-key` | Evaluate the real model on fixed maintenance, product-drift, and test-fakery cases; no GitHub writes |
| `check-provider` | `provider-key` | Verify the key shape (no whitespace, line break or quotes), DeepSeek authentication and JSON output without touching a PR |
| `reconcile-base` | `config`, optional `update-token` | When the base moved (a push for human merges; a completed `pull_request_target` review run of a now-merged PR, a schedule or a dispatch for bot merges, which raise no push event), update (with an independent credential) or post a needs-branch-update notice on every approved PR it left behind; approves and merges nothing |
| `request-reassessment` | `config`, optional `pull-request` | Validate the maintainer trigger (or a completed PR verification `workflow_run`) and rerun the exact trusted PR metadata workflow; never rebuild contributor code |
| `plan-wiki` | `provider-key`, `wiki-config`, wiki/source checkouts | Generate and validate a coordinated multi-page draft after deployment; `wiki-draft: true` permits read-only validation |
| `evaluate-wiki` | `provider-key` | Read-only live factual checks on supported and deliberately false documentation |
| `publish-wiki` | `wiki-config`, validated `wiki-plan-path`, wiki/source checkouts | Revalidate deployment and publish every page in one non-force wiki commit; no provider key |
| `finalize` | `config`, `assessment` | Wait for GitHub auto-merge after the required native gate finishes, then preserve the existing CD handoff |

The wait is cheap and rate-limit aware: a running verification is polled every 15 s, an absent or queued one at growing gaps (15, 30, 60, then 120 s; about 10 requests for the default grace instead of 60), and the workflow-run listing is a conditional request (`If-None-Match`; a 304 does not count against the primary limit). A 403/429 (retry-after, `x-ratelimit-remaining`/`reset`, secondary or abuse limit) is retried with bounded exponential backoff and jitter that respects the stated reset. If the budget stays exhausted past the bounded wait, the review ends in an explicit hold, `Held: GitHub API rate limit, will retry after <time>`, shown in the `clouseau-review-incomplete` comment (`github_rate_limit`) and in the `retry_after` output; the next verification completion or a re-run after that time reassesses the PR.

# Automatic CI upgrades

Clouseau's protected review workflow uses the shared protocol below. Palazzo
and Colombo enable it through their own protected workflow installation PRs;
the shared release alone does not install consumer CI.
“Latest” means the commit returned for `gaulatti/clouseau`'s protected `main`
when the workflow's isolated `resolve-clouseau` job starts. It does not mean a
release tag, a contributor branch, or an unmerged candidate. Protection and the
central review process authorize that source; signatures retain their existing
workstation trust boundary.

The small `scripts/resolve` bootstrap is referenced in trusted consumer workflow
configuration as `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main`, never a commit pin, tag, other
branch or fork. The engine itself is resolved from protected main at run time and runs with
the repository's secrets, so a commit pin on the small bootstrap adds little protection and
only creates stale pins; following main also means a bootstrap maintenance change reaches
consumers without an installation PR. An existing full-commit reference keeps working, but
new installations use `@main`. It has no source-selection inputs. It checks the public GitHub
branch response, requires protected main and a full lowercase commit SHA, checks
out that SHA without persisted credentials, and computes the engine content
digest from that actual source. Unavailable, malformed and unprotected results
fail the workflow. There is no previous-version fallback or private dependency.

Every engine job directly needs that resolver and checks out its SHA. Jobs pass
`CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA` and `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST` from those job outputs; the
local action verifies the actual content and, when available, checkout commit.
Bootstrap identification checks the clean revision both before and after hashing.
These are trusted workflow values, never PR text or uploaded evidence. Git-free
action bundles verify their content digest against the same immutable selection.
Missing resolver output selects an invalid all-zero commit at checkout, so it
cannot silently select a default branch. The required approval job also fails
when resolution prevents assessment.
Tests of Clouseau itself still exercise proposed code; ordinary protected review
uses central main. The existing explicit owner-authorized installation path is
separate from automatic source selection. Explicit controller-installation pushes
skip the automatic resolver and use only their guarded, frozen candidate. They
do not publish an unused protected-main selection as their engine evidence.

GitHub action `uses` references cannot select a revision from runtime outputs.

Automatic integrations reference the stable bootstrap as `scripts/resolve@main`, resolve protected
Clouseau main once and use its frozen SHA and computed digest throughout the
workflow. [Automatic CI upgrades](automatic-ci-upgrades.md) bind receipts,
assessment, scoring, approval and merge to that selection; normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest PR. Legacy fixed installations retain
their explicit full-commit pin; new installations use `@main`. Both required native checks must
come from GitHub Actions; main requires strict up-to-date checks, stale-review
dismissal, last-push approval, no deletion, no force pushes and no bypass actors.
The installing administrator verifies those settings; routine tokens do not
receive repository administration permission.

Merge, deployment, live health and post-deployment wiki publication remain
separate results. This protocol preserves their existing handoff and never
declares delivery merely because a PR merged.

The inspector selects source IDs and line ranges. The controller supplies their
literal text, derives unit paths from complete file accounting, and derives every
technical finding's path from a concrete changed-source anchor. Atomic defect
grading always receives that causal anchor together with the factor's citations.
These fields cannot be invented independently by a model.

Use the `evaluate-acceptance` action operation with both provider keys for the
read-only eight-case qualification, including multi-file maintenance with executed
tests and corresponding documentation. Its complete artifact is written to
`work/acceptance-evaluation.json` in the caller's workspace; upload it with an
`always()` step. Passing synthetic cases is qualification evidence, not proof of
a genuine unattended merge or automatic repair.
The known-defect case requires a separate bounded Jev adjudication against its
frozen trigger, causal regression and forbidden outcome. An unrelated blocking
finding in the same file cannot qualify detection. The original findings,
reference, adjudication and binding digest remain in the artifact. A transport
fixture tests framing only and never substitutes for this live judgment.

A purpose handoff must accompany a capability whose upper fit is below 80.
An inspector's request to authorize an internal framework cannot itself make
that framework a product direction; unnecessary machinery remains repair work.
Technical necessity and severity are graded for distinct runtime, data, security,
compatibility, or verification consequences. Product scope and proportionality
are still enforced by the independent product scores and scope gate.

# Initial consumer trust installation

Ordinary review reads its recipe and public signing enrollment from accepted
base configuration. A consumer with neither file needs a separate initial
trust decision. Never pretend proposed configuration is accepted, repeatedly
invoke a normal review that cannot bootstrap, or substitute an unsigned report
for an approval receipt.

These explicit installation commands are independent of agent startup. They use
the existing authenticated Codex or Claude Code harness and Ed25519 identity,
not CI model keys or a new credential service.

## Freeze and explicitly authorize initial trust

1. Read the accepted requirement and repository purpose. Preserve existing
   controls and ownership. Prepare real complete verification before trust.
2. Obtain the shared engine identity and the runner's public enrollment:

   ```sh
   clouseau installation-engine
   clouseau public-identity
   ```

   Select `--identity /outside/project/identity.json` when necessary. If none
   exists, explicitly run `clouseau init-identity` first. Public export returns
   only the enrollment and local identity-file path. Never copy private material
   into source, prompts, logs or artifacts.
3. Prepare the supported local recipe, version-two CI policy, purpose,
   ownership and thin workflows. The proposed CI policy must enroll that one
   public identity for its native GitHub actor, authorize the fixed public
   `central_source` from the [released upgrade protocol](automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
   or name the reported legacy engine digest, and select that actor as manual
   reviewer. The initial manifest and receipt always bind one exact engine SHA
   and digest, including in central-source mode. Commit and push the complete
   candidate. Store the literal accepted requirement outside the checkout.
   Keep the accepted base branch (`main`) free of `.clouseau-local.json` and
   `.github/clouseau.json`: push the candidate on its own branch (for example
   `install/clouseau`) and open the PR from it. The full commit SHA to pin in
   the `initial-trust` workflow checkout (`FULL_REVIEWED_RELEASE_SHA` below) is the

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly
the head source with every line prefixed `+` (consumers restore the identical patch). The pinned
engine seed (roughly 380 KB) is collected only when a workflow change adds or changes a
`gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main` (or an existing `@<sha>`) reference; an ordinary edit of a workflow that keeps its reference
carries no engine source, and a reviewer can still request any of it. The seed is optional context: seed files that would use the last 150,000
characters are listed in `omitted_sources` with a reason, and reviewers can still request them.
Changed files, their base and head sources and contracts are never omitted; a change that exceeds
the cap with only that evidence is reviewed in bounded units (see "Chunked local review") unless the protected configuration disabled chunked review, in which case it fails closed.

## Enrolling a trusted runner

Consumers with neither accepted recipe nor CI policy use the separate
[explicit initial trust installation](initial-installation.md). Its frozen
owner/admin commit-comment grant and installation-only evidence cannot replace
ordinary approval or authorize automatic merge.

`clouseau init-identity` creates an Ed25519 identity outside the repository with
private file permissions. Its output contains only the public enrollment entry
and local identity-file path. Identity creation is explicit and is never part of
agent installation. The existing authenticated GitHub account supplies the
identity's `github_actor`.

An owner must install the public enrollment entry in protected CI configuration:


## Operations

Automatic CI integrations pin the small `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve`
bootstrap once at a reviewed full commit. It selects protected Clouseau main,
freezes its SHA and computes its digest. Every engine job checks out that SHA
and invokes the local action with the same trusted outputs. Normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest update. See [automatic CI upgrades](docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
for source authorization, failure behavior and exact local-receipt compatibility.
Legacy fixed installations may still use `gaulatti/clouseau@FULL_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA`;
upgrading those installations requires a reviewed PR. See `examples/colombo.json`
for the version 2 policy configuration.

| Operation | Inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verify-engine` | Trusted run SHA/digest in `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA` and `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST` | Verify the frozen source and record its exact identity |
| `test` | none | Run Clouseau's Node regression suite |
| `coverage` | Accepted-base v2 `coverage-config`, or legacy `coverage-report` + `source-directory` with optional `coverage-format` | Require exact, nonempty 100% native application line and branch coverage; the two input forms are mutually exclusive. A repository can opt in to [changed-line coverage](docs/changed-line-coverage.md) with `coverage.mode` in its protected config plus `coverage-base-ref` and `coverage-baseline` |
| `await-verification` | `config`, `pull-request` for non-PR events | Wait for the exact-head PR verification run without deadlocking a single-slot runner pool: ends cleanly with `verified=false` when verification has not started within `verification_queue_grace_seconds` (default 900), to be reassessed when the verification run completes |
| `assess` | `config`, optional `pull-request`, `provider-key`, optional `ignore-receipt: 'true'` (never read the PR's receipt; for the hosted fallback after an unusable receipt) | Authenticate local quality evidence independently of technical status, or wait for verification before CI AI assessment |
| `verify-local` | `config`, eligible published signed receipt | Validate local evidence and independent CI with zero AI calls; missing or invalid evidence holds |
| `gate` | `config`, `assessment`, optional `pull-request` | Validate protection, arm auto-merge, request owner review, or approve a verified revision |
| `repair` | v2 `config`, `assessment`, this run's record artifacts, independent `repair-token` | Validate and reserve one bounded correction, then push a new internal PR revision requiring fresh CI/review |
| `evaluate-acceptance` | `provider-key`, `typesafe-key` | Execute six fixed qualification fixtures, investigate with real models, compare DeepSeek and Jev grading plus whole-review cost; retain evidence without GitHub writes |
| `evaluate-review` | `provider-key` | Evaluate the real model on fixed maintenance, product-drift, and test-fakery cases; no GitHub writes |
| `check-provider` | `provider-key` | Verify the key shape (no whitespace, line break or quotes), DeepSeek authentication and JSON output without touching a PR |
| `reconcile-base` | `config`, optional `update-token` | When the base moved (a push for human merges; a completed `pull_request_target` review run of a now-merged PR, a schedule or a dispatch for bot merges, which raise no push event), update (with an independent credential) or post a needs-branch-update notice on every approved PR it left behind; approves and merges nothing |
| `request-reassessment` | `config`, optional `pull-request` | Validate the maintainer trigger (or a completed PR verification `workflow_run`) and rerun the exact trusted PR metadata workflow; never rebuild contributor code |
| `plan-wiki` | `provider-key`, `wiki-config`, wiki/source checkouts | Generate and validate a coordinated multi-page draft after deployment; `wiki-draft: true` permits read-only validation |
| `evaluate-wiki` | `provider-key` | Read-only live factual checks on supported and deliberately false documentation |
| `publish-wiki` | `wiki-config`, validated `wiki-plan-path`, wiki/source checkouts | Revalidate deployment and publish every page in one non-force wiki commit; no provider key |
| `finalize` | `config`, `assessment` | Wait for GitHub auto-merge after the required native gate finishes, then preserve the existing CD handoff |

The wait is cheap and rate-limit aware: a running verification is polled every 15 s, an absent or queued one at growing gaps (15, 30, 60, then 120 s; about 10 requests for the default grace instead of 60), and the workflow-run listing is a conditional request (`If-None-Match`; a 304 does not count against the primary limit). A 403/429 (retry-after, `x-ratelimit-remaining`/`reset`, secondary or abuse limit) is retried with bounded exponential backoff and jitter that respects the stated reset. If the budget stays exhausted past the bounded wait, the review ends in an explicit hold, `Held: GitHub API rate limit, will retry after <time>`, shown in the `clouseau-review-incomplete` comment (`github_rate_limit`) and in the `retry_after` output; the next verification completion or a re-run after that time reassesses the PR.

# Automatic CI upgrades

Clouseau's protected review workflow uses the shared protocol below. Palazzo
and Colombo enable it through their own protected workflow installation PRs;
the shared release alone does not install consumer CI.
“Latest” means the commit returned for `gaulatti/clouseau`'s protected `main`
when the workflow's isolated `resolve-clouseau` job starts. It does not mean a
release tag, a contributor branch, or an unmerged candidate. Protection and the
central review process authorize that source; signatures retain their existing
workstation trust boundary.

The small `scripts/resolve` bootstrap is pinned once in trusted consumer workflow
configuration. It has no source-selection inputs. It checks the public GitHub
branch response, requires protected main and a full lowercase commit SHA, checks
out that SHA without persisted credentials, and computes the engine content
digest from that actual source. Unavailable, malformed and unprotected results
fail the workflow. There is no previous-version fallback or private dependency.

Every engine job directly needs that resolver and checks out its SHA. Jobs pass
`CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA` and `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST` from those job outputs; the
local action verifies the actual content and, when available, checkout commit.
Bootstrap identification checks the clean revision both before and after hashing.
These are trusted workflow values, never PR text or uploaded evidence. Git-free
action bundles verify their content digest against the same immutable selection.
Missing resolver output selects an invalid all-zero commit at checkout, so it
cannot silently select a default branch. The required approval job also fails
when resolution prevents assessment.
Tests of Clouseau itself still exercise proposed code; ordinary protected review
uses central main. The existing explicit owner-authorized installation path is
separate from automatic source selection. Explicit controller-installation pushes
skip the automatic resolver and use only their guarded, frozen candidate. They
do not publish an unused protected-main selection as their engine evidence.

GitHub action `uses` references cannot select a revision from runtime outputs.
Use a literal local action path after `actions/checkout` with an expression in
`with.ref`. Do not resolve main independently in each job. See GitHub's
[workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idstepsuses)
and [context availability](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#context-availability).

Assessment outputs and acceptance artifacts bind the frozen SHA and computed

Automatic integrations pin a reviewed stable bootstrap, resolve protected
Clouseau main once and use its frozen SHA and computed digest throughout the
workflow. [Automatic CI upgrades](automatic-ci-upgrades.md) bind receipts,
assessment, scoring, approval and merge to that selection; normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest PR. Legacy fixed installations retain
their explicit full-commit pin. Both required native checks must
come from GitHub Actions; main requires strict up-to-date checks, stale-review
dismissal, last-push approval, no deletion, no force pushes and no bypass actors.
The installing administrator verifies those settings; routine tokens do not
receive repository administration permission.

Merge, deployment, live health and post-deployment wiki publication remain
separate results. This protocol preserves their existing handoff and never
declares delivery merely because a PR merged.

The inspector selects source IDs and line ranges. The controller supplies their
literal text, derives unit paths from complete file accounting, and derives every
technical finding's path from a concrete changed-source anchor. Atomic defect
grading always receives that causal anchor together with the factor's citations.
These fields cannot be invented independently by a model.

Use the `evaluate-acceptance` action operation with both provider keys for the
read-only eight-case qualification, including multi-file maintenance with executed
tests and corresponding documentation. Its complete artifact is written to
`work/acceptance-evaluation.json` in the caller's workspace; upload it with an
`always()` step. Passing synthetic cases is qualification evidence, not proof of
a genuine unattended merge or automatic repair.
The known-defect case requires a separate bounded Jev adjudication against its
frozen trigger, causal regression and forbidden outcome. An unrelated blocking
finding in the same file cannot qualify detection. The original findings,
reference, adjudication and binding digest remain in the artifact. A transport
fixture tests framing only and never substitutes for this live judgment.

A purpose handoff must accompany a capability whose upper fit is below 80.
An inspector's request to authorize an internal framework cannot itself make
that framework a product direction; unnecessary machinery remains repair work.
Technical necessity and severity are graded for distinct runtime, data, security,
compatibility, or verification consequences. Product scope and proportionality
are still enforced by the independent product scores and scope gate.

# Initial consumer trust installation

Ordinary review reads its recipe and public signing enrollment from accepted
base configuration. A consumer with neither file needs a separate initial
trust decision. Never pretend proposed configuration is accepted, repeatedly
invoke a normal review that cannot bootstrap, or substitute an unsigned report
for an approval receipt.

These explicit installation commands are independent of agent startup. They use
the existing authenticated Codex or Claude Code harness and Ed25519 identity,
not CI model keys or a new credential service.

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly
the head source with every line prefixed `+` (consumers restore the identical patch). The pinned
engine seed (roughly 380 KB) is collected only when a workflow change adds or changes a
`gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@<sha>` pin; an ordinary edit of a workflow that keeps its pin
carries no engine source, and a reviewer can still request any of it. The seed is optional context: seed files that would use the last 150,000
characters are listed in `omitted_sources` with a reason, and reviewers can still request them.
Changed files, their base and head sources and contracts are never omitted; a change that exceeds
the cap with only that evidence is reviewed in bounded units (see "Chunked local review") unless the protected configuration disabled chunked review, in which case it fails closed.

There is no application-specific deployment infrastructure in Clouseau.

## Operations

Automatic CI integrations reference the small `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main`
bootstrap, so it always follows the latest protected main (the engine is resolved from protected
main at run time with the repository's secrets, so a commit pin on the bootstrap adds little and
only goes stale). It selects protected Clouseau main,
freezes its SHA and computes its digest. Every engine job checks out that SHA
and invokes the local action with the same trusted outputs. Normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest update; existing full-commit references keep working. See [automatic CI upgrades](docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
for source authorization, failure behavior and exact local-receipt compatibility.
Legacy fixed installations may still use `gaulatti/clouseau@FULL_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA`;
upgrading those installations requires a reviewed PR. See `examples/colombo.json`
for the version 2 policy configuration.

| Operation | Inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verify-engine` | Trusted run SHA/digest in `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA` and `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST` | Verify the frozen source and record its exact identity |
| `test` | none | Run Clouseau's Node regression suite |
| `coverage` | Accepted-base v2 `coverage-config`, or legacy `coverage-report` + `source-directory` with optional `coverage-format` | Require exact, nonempty 100% native application line and branch coverage; the two input forms are mutually exclusive. A repository can opt in to [changed-line coverage](docs/changed-line-coverage.md) with `coverage.mode` in its protected config plus `coverage-base-ref` and `coverage-baseline` |
| `await-verification` | `config`, `pull-request` for non-PR events | Wait for the exact-head PR verification run without deadlocking a single-slot runner pool: ends cleanly with `verified=false` when verification has not started within `verification_queue_grace_seconds` (default 900), to be reassessed when the verification run completes |
| `assess` | `config`, optional `pull-request`, `provider-key`, optional `ignore-receipt: 'true'` (never read the PR's receipt; for the hosted fallback after an unusable receipt) | Authenticate local quality evidence independently of technical status, or wait for verification before CI AI assessment |
| `verify-local` | `config`, eligible published signed receipt | Validate local evidence and independent CI with zero AI calls; missing or invalid evidence holds |
| `gate` | `config`, `assessment`, optional `pull-request` | Validate protection, arm auto-merge, request owner review, or approve a verified revision |
| `repair` | v2 `config`, `assessment`, this run's record artifacts, independent `repair-token` | Validate and reserve one bounded correction, then push a new internal PR revision requiring fresh CI/review |
| `evaluate-acceptance` | `provider-key`, `typesafe-key` | Execute six fixed qualification fixtures, investigate with real models, compare DeepSeek and Jev grading plus whole-review cost; retain evidence without GitHub writes |
| `evaluate-review` | `provider-key` | Evaluate the real model on fixed maintenance, product-drift, and test-fakery cases; no GitHub writes |
| `check-provider` | `provider-key` | Verify the key shape (no whitespace, line break or quotes), DeepSeek authentication and JSON output without touching a PR |
| `reconcile-base` | `config`, optional `update-token` | When the base moved (a push for human merges; a completed `pull_request_target` review run of a now-merged PR, a schedule or a dispatch for bot merges, which raise no push event), update (with an independent credential) or post a needs-branch-update notice on every approved PR it left behind; approves and merges nothing |
| `request-reassessment` | `config`, optional `pull-request` | Validate the maintainer trigger (or a completed PR verification `workflow_run`) and rerun the exact trusted PR metadata workflow; never rebuild contributor code |
| `plan-wiki` | `provider-key`, `wiki-config`, wiki/source checkouts | Generate and validate a coordinated multi-page draft after deployment; `wiki-draft: true` permits read-only validation |
| `evaluate-wiki` | `provider-key` | Read-only live factual checks on supported and deliberately false documentation |
| `publish-wiki` | `wiki-config`, validated `wiki-plan-path`, wiki/source checkouts | Revalidate deployment and publish every page in one non-force wiki commit; no provider key |
| `finalize` | `config`, `assessment` | Wait for GitHub auto-merge after the required native gate finishes, then preserve the existing CD handoff |

The wait is cheap and rate-limit aware: a running verification is polled every 15 s, an absent or queued one at growing gaps (15, 30, 60, then 120 s; about 10 requests for the default grace instead of 60), and the workflow-run listing is a conditional request (`If-None-Match`; a 304 does not count against the primary limit). A 403/429 (retry-after, `x-ratelimit-remaining`/`reset`, secondary or abuse limit) is retried with bounded exponential backoff and jitter that respects the stated reset. If the budget stays exhausted past the bounded wait, the review ends in an explicit hold, `Held: GitHub API rate limit, will retry after <time>`, shown in the `clouseau-review-incomplete` comment (`github_rate_limit`) and in the `retry_after` output; the next verification completion or a re-run after that time reassesses the PR.

# Automatic CI upgrades

Clouseau's protected review workflow uses the shared protocol below. Palazzo
and Colombo enable it through their own protected workflow installation PRs;
the shared release alone does not install consumer CI.
“Latest” means the commit returned for `gaulatti/clouseau`'s protected `main`
when the workflow's isolated `resolve-clouseau` job starts. It does not mean a
release tag, a contributor branch, or an unmerged candidate. Protection and the
central review process authorize that source; signatures retain their existing
workstation trust boundary.

The small `scripts/resolve` bootstrap is referenced in trusted consumer workflow
configuration as `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main`, never a commit pin, tag, other
branch or fork. The engine itself is resolved from protected main at run time and runs with
the repository's secrets, so a commit pin on the small bootstrap adds little protection and
only creates stale pins; following main also means a bootstrap maintenance change reaches
consumers without an installation PR. An existing full-commit reference keeps working, but
new installations use `@main`. It has no source-selection inputs. It checks the public GitHub
branch response, requires protected main and a full lowercase commit SHA, checks
out that SHA without persisted credentials, and computes the engine content
digest from that actual source. Unavailable, malformed and unprotected results
fail the workflow. There is no previous-version fallback or private dependency.

Every engine job directly needs that resolver and checks out its SHA. Jobs pass
`CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA` and `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST` from those job outputs; the
local action verifies the actual content and, when available, checkout commit.
Bootstrap identification checks the clean revision both before and after hashing.
These are trusted workflow values, never PR text or uploaded evidence. Git-free
action bundles verify their content digest against the same immutable selection.
Missing resolver output selects an invalid all-zero commit at checkout, so it
cannot silently select a default branch. The required approval job also fails
when resolution prevents assessment.
Tests of Clouseau itself still exercise proposed code; ordinary protected review
uses central main. The existing explicit owner-authorized installation path is
separate from automatic source selection. Explicit controller-installation pushes
skip the automatic resolver and use only their guarded, frozen candidate. They
do not publish an unused protected-main selection as their engine evidence.

GitHub action `uses` references cannot select a revision from runtime outputs.
Use a literal local action path after `actions/checkout` with an expression in

cannot waive tests, coverage, integrity failures or technical repairs.

Before the AI assessment, the controller reads the configured human owner's
exact-revision intent comment and verifies current write, maintain or admin
permission through GitHub. The literal receipt becomes a content-addressed,
trusted contract source in the proof catalog. This records accepted purpose,
not an approval score: all technical and integrity gates remain mandatory. Contributor claims and issue text do not acquire contract authority.
Before any approval write, the gate checks that a receipt used in the assessment
still exists unchanged and that its author remains authorized. Removed, altered
or revoked confirmation requires reassessment rather than reusing a stale score.

Clouseau's own reviewer upgrades have a separate owner-authorized installation
route so a defective installed reviewer cannot prevent installing its verified
replacement. First qualify the frozen candidate and confirm its exact PR head.
The owner then publishes that commit to `policy-install/pr-NUMBER`:

```sh
git push origin FULL_HEAD_SHA:refs/heads/policy-install/pr-NUMBER
```

Before loading the candidate controller, a read-only guard requires the owner
actor, owner-authored open non-draft PR, the same repository, `main` as its base,
an exact matching head SHA and the owner's exact-revision intent comment.
The separate read-only AI assessment and write gate use that frozen revision.
They retain the full scored protocol, fresh PR verification, exact coverage,
evidence/history checks, native approval and existing branch protection. Failed
preparation or assessment fails the required approval job. Ordinary PR events
always load the controller from protected `main`; fork PRs cannot use this route.
Deleting an installation branch starts no installation or approval work.

The read-only assessment uploads its full source-bound record and emits a compact
digest. The separate approval job downloads that run's artifact, checks the
digest, recomputes scores, reconciles history and rechecks current CI/head/base.
It then records fresh approval and arms native auto-merge only when effective
protection and repository auto-merge are present; otherwise it posts one
fixed-text notice naming the missing setting classes, withholds the merge and
the job still succeeds (see the README). No provider key enters the approval or repair writer. The author
token enters only the repair writer. Same-revision intent comments reassess
metadata without rebuilding the application container.

Automatic integrations reference the stable bootstrap as `scripts/resolve@main`, resolve protected
Clouseau main once and use its frozen SHA and computed digest throughout the
workflow. [Automatic CI upgrades](automatic-ci-upgrades.md) bind receipts,
assessment, scoring, approval and merge to that selection; normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest PR. Legacy fixed installations retain
their explicit full-commit pin; new installations use `@main`. Both required native checks must
come from GitHub Actions; main requires strict up-to-date checks, stale-review
dismissal, last-push approval, no deletion, no force pushes and no bypass actors.
The installing administrator verifies those settings; routine tokens do not
receive repository administration permission.

Merge, deployment, live health and post-deployment wiki publication remain
separate results. This protocol preserves their existing handoff and never
declares delivery merely because a PR merged.

The inspector selects source IDs and line ranges. The controller supplies their
literal text, derives unit paths from complete file accounting, and derives every
technical finding's path from a concrete changed-source anchor. Atomic defect
grading always receives that causal anchor together with the factor's citations.
These fields cannot be invented independently by a model.

Use the `evaluate-acceptance` action operation with both provider keys for the
read-only eight-case qualification, including multi-file maintenance with executed
tests and corresponding documentation. Its complete artifact is written to
`work/acceptance-evaluation.json` in the caller's workspace; upload it with an
`always()` step. Passing synthetic cases is qualification evidence, not proof of
a genuine unattended merge or automatic repair.
The known-defect case requires a separate bounded Jev adjudication against its
frozen trigger, causal regression and forbidden outcome. An unrelated blocking
finding in the same file cannot qualify detection. The original findings,
reference, adjudication and binding digest remain in the artifact. A transport
fixture tests framing only and never substitutes for this live judgment.

A purpose handoff must accompany a capability whose upper fit is below 80.
An inspector's request to authorize an internal framework cannot itself make
that framework a product direction; unnecessary machinery remains repair work.
Technical necessity and severity are graded for distinct runtime, data, security,
compatibility, or verification consequences. Product scope and proportionality
are still enforced by the independent product scores and scope gate.

# Initial consumer trust installation

Ordinary review reads its recipe and public signing enrollment from accepted
base configuration. A consumer with neither file needs a separate initial
trust decision. Never pretend proposed configuration is accepted, repeatedly
invoke a normal review that cannot bootstrap, or substitute an unsigned report
for an approval receipt.

These explicit installation commands are independent of agent startup. They use
the existing authenticated Codex or Claude Code harness and Ed25519 identity,
not CI model keys or a new credential service.

## Freeze and explicitly authorize initial trust

1. Read the accepted requirement and repository purpose. Preserve existing
   controls and ownership. Prepare real complete verification before trust.
2. Obtain the shared engine identity and the runner's public enrollment:

   ```sh
   clouseau installation-engine
   clouseau public-identity
   ```

   Select `--identity /outside/project/identity.json` when necessary. If none
   exists, explicitly run `clouseau init-identity` first. Public export returns
   only the enrollment and local identity-file path. Never copy private material
   into source, prompts, logs or artifacts.
3. Prepare the supported local recipe, version-two CI policy, purpose,
   ownership and thin workflows. The proposed CI policy must enroll that one
   public identity for its native GitHub actor, authorize the fixed public
   `central_source` from the [released upgrade protocol](automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
   or name the reported legacy engine digest, and select that actor as manual
   reviewer. The initial manifest and receipt always bind one exact engine SHA
   and digest, including in central-source mode. Commit and push the complete
   candidate. Store the literal accepted requirement outside the checkout.
   Keep the accepted base branch (`main`) free of `.clouseau-local.json` and
   `.github/clouseau.json`: push the candidate on its own branch (for example
   `install/clouseau`) and open the PR from it. The full commit SHA to pin in
   the `initial-trust` workflow checkout (`FULL_REVIEWED_RELEASE_SHA` below) is the
   `reviewer_sha` printed by `clouseau installation-engine`. The CI workflow's bootstrap is

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly
the head source with every line prefixed `+` (consumers restore the identical patch). The pinned
engine seed (roughly 380 KB) is collected only when a workflow change adds or changes a
`gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main` (or an existing `@<sha>`) reference; an ordinary edit of a workflow that keeps its reference
carries no engine source, and a reviewer can still request any of it. The seed is optional context: seed files that would use the last 150,000
characters are listed in `omitted_sources` with a reason, and reviewers can still request them.
Changed files, their base and head sources and contracts are never omitted; a change that exceeds
the cap with only that evidence is reviewed in bounded units (see "Chunked local review") unless the protected configuration disabled chunked review, in which case it fails closed.

## Enrolling a trusted runner

Consumers with neither accepted recipe nor CI policy use the separate
[explicit initial trust installation](initial-installation.md). Its frozen
owner/admin commit-comment grant and installation-only evidence cannot replace
ordinary approval or authorize automatic merge.

`clouseau init-identity` creates an Ed25519 identity outside the repository with
private file permissions. Its output contains only the public enrollment entry
and local identity-file path. Identity creation is explicit and is never part of
agent installation. The existing authenticated GitHub account supplies the
identity's `github_actor`.

An owner must install the public enrollment entry in protected CI configuration:

```json
{
  "local_review": {
    "mode": "required",
    "central_source": {"repository": "gaulatti/clouseau", "ref": "refs/heads/main"},
    "max_age_seconds": 172800,
    "keys": [{
      "id": "PUBLIC_KEY_IDENTIFIER",
      "issuer": "ENROLLED_RUNNER_IDENTIFIER",
      "github_actor": "ENROLLED_GITHUB_LOGIN",

clouseau public-identity        # the public enrollment for clouseau.json
```

Keep `main` free of `.clouseau-local.json` and `.github/clouseau.json`. On a new
branch (for example `install/clouseau`) add:

- `.clouseau-local.json` as **version 2** (CI's `coverage-config` accepts only
  version 2; see [local review](local-review.md#multiple-native-coverage-artifacts)),
- `.github/clouseau.json` from [`examples/consumer-clouseau.json`](../examples/consumer-clouseau.json)
  with your public enrollment, owner and verification step names,
- `.github/clouseau.md` (the purpose contract) and `.github/CODEOWNERS`,
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` from [`examples/consumer-ci.yml`](../examples/consumer-ci.yml)
  and the `initial-trust` workflow from [initial installation](initial-installation.md#independent-ci-and-initial-owner-acceptance),
  The `ci.yml` bootstrap is referenced as `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main` (never a
  commit, tag or other branch: the engine is resolved from protected main at run time, so a
  commit pin on the bootstrap adds little and only goes stale). Only the `initial-trust`
  workflow's `shared-clouseau` checkout is pinned to the `reviewer_sha`.

A repository far below 100% coverage can add `"coverage": {"mode": "changed_lines"}`
to `.github/clouseau.json` to gate changed lines instead; see
[changed-line coverage](changed-line-coverage.md). The default stays exact 100%.

## 3. Initial trust PR

Follow [initial installation](initial-installation.md): `installation-prepare`,
`installation-authorize`, `installation-review --harness claude|codex`,
`installation-publish`, then open the PR from the install branch with the
returned marker in its body. Wait for `verify` and `initial-trust`, then merge it
yourself: initial trust never auto-merges.

# Clouseau

Clouseau also provides a centrally maintained local agent skill and signed review
receipts. Agent-only installation is independent of CI: it uses authenticated
coding harnesses and creates no Actions configuration or provider secrets.
Inside Claude Code, Codex or opencode the calling agent supplies the review
sessions (`--agent`); the headless `--harness` form is for a plain terminal.
Local AI review runs regardless of coverage percentage or availability and keeps
its quality verdict separate from real verification results. Opted-in CI verifies
an enrolled runner's passing AI receipt without repeating the review, then still
requires its own tests and exact coverage before approval/merge. See
[local review, installation and trust boundaries](docs/local-review.md).
New to Clouseau? Start with the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md).
How a receipt stays valid across engine revisions: [receipt compatibility](docs/receipt-compatibility.md).
Every refusal or hold notice names its cause class and numbered next steps: [notices and their causes](docs/notices.md).
Consumers without accepted recipe/enrollment/workflows use the separate
[initial owner-authorized trust installation](docs/initial-installation.md).
Its signed evidence cannot approve ordinary changes or automatically merge.
Clouseau's own accepted-policy bootstrap and native coverage diagnostics are
documented in [self-review](docs/self-review.md).

Shared coverage gates and evidence-led AI pull request approval for GitHub Actions.
Clouseau owns the PR intent review process: check whether a change is needed,
compare it with repository contracts and precedent, request the owner's second
opinion when necessary, and approve and arm auto-merge only after every technical
requirement passes. The initial implementation was extracted from Colombo.

Version 2 implements the [change acceptance protocol](docs/change-acceptance.md):
product fit, need and proportionality; nine-factor technical findings; independent
source investigations; a persistent evidence ledger; bounded repairs; and native
protected auto-merge. Humans decide genuine purpose and authority questions.
Technical uncertainty goes to automated investigation and cannot be waived by
an intent comment. Version 1 remains explicit compatibility for existing pins.

## Ownership

Clouseau contains the coverage checker, regression tests, PR intent review rules,
DeepSeek integration, approval controller, and reusable composite action.
Each consuming repository keeps its build/test commands, a configuration file,
and its own purpose, contracts, acceptance criteria, and manual-review owner.

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

# Automatic CI upgrades

Clouseau's protected review workflow uses the shared protocol below. Palazzo
and Colombo enable it through their own protected workflow installation PRs;
the shared release alone does not install consumer CI.
“Latest” means the commit returned for `gaulatti/clouseau`'s protected `main`
when the workflow's isolated `resolve-clouseau` job starts. It does not mean a
release tag, a contributor branch, or an unmerged candidate. Protection and the
central review process authorize that source; signatures retain their existing
workstation trust boundary.

The small `scripts/resolve` bootstrap is pinned once in trusted consumer workflow
configuration. It has no source-selection inputs. It checks the public GitHub
branch response, requires protected main and a full lowercase commit SHA, checks
out that SHA without persisted credentials, and computes the engine content
digest from that actual source. Unavailable, malformed and unprotected results
fail the workflow. There is no previous-version fallback or private dependency.

Every engine job directly needs that resolver and checks out its SHA. Jobs pass
`CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA` and `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST` from those job outputs; the
local action verifies the actual content and, when available, checkout commit.
Bootstrap identification checks the clean revision both before and after hashing.
These are trusted workflow values, never PR text or uploaded evidence. Git-free
action bundles verify their content digest against the same immutable selection.
Missing resolver output selects an invalid all-zero commit at checkout, so it
cannot silently select a default branch. The required approval job also fails
when resolution prevents assessment.
Tests of Clouseau itself still exercise proposed code; ordinary protected review
uses central main. The existing explicit owner-authorized installation path is
separate from automatic source selection. Explicit controller-installation pushes
skip the automatic resolver and use only their guarded, frozen candidate. They
do not publish an unused protected-main selection as their engine evidence.

GitHub action `uses` references cannot select a revision from runtime outputs.
Use a literal local action path after `actions/checkout` with an expression in
`with.ref`. Do not resolve main independently in each job. See GitHub's
[workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idstepsuses)
and [context availability](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#context-availability).

Assessment outputs and acceptance artifacts bind the frozen SHA and computed

cannot waive tests, coverage, integrity failures or technical repairs.

Before the AI assessment, the controller reads the configured human owner's
exact-revision intent comment and verifies current write, maintain or admin
permission through GitHub. The literal receipt becomes a content-addressed,
trusted contract source in the proof catalog. This records accepted purpose,
not an approval score: all technical and integrity gates remain mandatory. Contributor claims and issue text do not acquire contract authority.
Before any approval write, the gate checks that a receipt used in the assessment
still exists unchanged and that its author remains authorized. Removed, altered
or revoked confirmation requires reassessment rather than reusing a stale score.

Clouseau's own reviewer upgrades have a separate owner-authorized installation
route so a defective installed reviewer cannot prevent installing its verified
replacement. First qualify the frozen candidate and confirm its exact PR head.
The owner then publishes that commit to `policy-install/pr-NUMBER`:

```sh
git push origin FULL_HEAD_SHA:refs/heads/policy-install/pr-NUMBER
```

Before loading the candidate controller, a read-only guard requires the owner
actor, owner-authored open non-draft PR, the same repository, `main` as its base,
an exact matching head SHA and the owner's exact-revision intent comment.
The separate read-only AI assessment and write gate use that frozen revision.
They retain the full scored protocol, fresh PR verification, exact coverage,
evidence/history checks, native approval and existing branch protection. Failed
preparation or assessment fails the required approval job. Ordinary PR events
always load the controller from protected `main`; fork PRs cannot use this route.
Deleting an installation branch starts no installation or approval work.

The read-only assessment uploads its full source-bound record and emits a compact
digest. The separate approval job downloads that run's artifact, checks the
digest, recomputes scores, reconciles history and rechecks current CI/head/base.
It then records fresh approval and arms native auto-merge only when effective
protection and repository auto-merge are present; otherwise it posts one
fixed-text notice naming the missing setting classes, withholds the merge and
the job still succeeds (see the README). No provider key enters the approval or repair writer. The author
token enters only the repair writer. Same-revision intent comments reassess
metadata without rebuilding the application container.

# Initial consumer trust installation

Ordinary review reads its recipe and public signing enrollment from accepted
base configuration. A consumer with neither file needs a separate initial
trust decision. Never pretend proposed configuration is accepted, repeatedly
invoke a normal review that cannot bootstrap, or substitute an unsigned report
for an approval receipt.

These explicit installation commands are independent of agent startup. They use
the existing authenticated Codex or Claude Code harness and Ed25519 identity,
not CI model keys or a new credential service.

## Freeze and explicitly authorize initial trust

1. Read the accepted requirement and repository purpose. Preserve existing
   controls and ownership. Prepare real complete verification before trust.
2. Obtain the shared engine identity and the runner's public enrollment:

   ```sh
   clouseau installation-engine
   clouseau public-identity
   ```

   Select `--identity /outside/project/identity.json` when necessary. If none
   exists, explicitly run `clouseau init-identity` first. Public export returns
   only the enrollment and local identity-file path. Never copy private material
   into source, prompts, logs or artifacts.
3. Prepare the supported local recipe, version-two CI policy, purpose,
   ownership and thin workflows. The proposed CI policy must enroll that one
   public identity for its native GitHub actor, authorize the fixed public
   `central_source` from the [released upgrade protocol](automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
   or name the reported legacy engine digest, and select that actor as manual

   candidate. Store the literal accepted requirement outside the checkout.
   Keep the accepted base branch (`main`) free of `.clouseau-local.json` and

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly
the head source with every line prefixed `+` (consumers restore the identical patch). The pinned
engine seed (roughly 380 KB) is collected only when a workflow change adds or changes a
`gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@<sha>` pin; an ordinary edit of a workflow that keeps its pin
carries no engine source, and a reviewer can still request any of it. The seed is optional context: seed files that would use the last 150,000
characters are listed in `omitted_sources` with a reason, and reviewers can still request them.
Changed files, their base and head sources and contracts are never omitted; a change that exceeds
the cap with only that evidence is reviewed in bounded units (see "Chunked local review") unless the protected configuration disabled chunked review, in which case it fails closed.

## Enrolling a trusted runner

Consumers with neither accepted recipe nor CI policy use the separate
[explicit initial trust installation](initial-installation.md). Its frozen
owner/admin commit-comment grant and installation-only evidence cannot replace
ordinary approval or authorize automatic merge.

`clouseau init-identity` creates an Ed25519 identity outside the repository with
private file permissions. Its output contains only the public enrollment entry
and local identity-file path. Identity creation is explicit and is never part of
agent installation. The existing authenticated GitHub account supplies the
identity's `github_actor`.

An owner must install the public enrollment entry in protected CI configuration:

# Quickstart: a new repository to its first auto-merged PR

This is the shortest verified path for a repository with no Clouseau files. It
links to the reference documents instead of repeating them. Every step below was
run in a fresh repository. Decide first which mode you want:

| Mode | You need | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local receipt (`local_review.mode: optional` or `required`) | An authenticated `codex` or `claude` on your workstation | The PR carries a signed local review; CI only verifies it. No provider key |
| CI review (PRs without a receipt, `optional` mode) | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` secret (and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` when `acceptance.grader` is `routed` or `typesafe`) | CI performs the AI review itself |

Without the CI secrets, a PR that has no valid receipt ends with the comment
`Clouseau review incomplete ... DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is not configured`; add the
secret and re-run the failed jobs.

## 1. Repository settings (before the first PR)

- Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions: enable **Allow GitHub
  Actions to create and approve pull requests** (API:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/permissions/workflow -F can_approve_pull_request_reviews=true -f default_workflow_permissions=read`).
  The automatic approval depends on it (see the README's protected-merge
  requirements).
- Settings > General > Pull Requests: enable **Allow auto-merge** and squash
  merging. Private repositories on a plan without branch protection cannot enable
  it; see [the private-plan path](change-acceptance.md#controller-enforced-owner-merge-on-an-unavailable-private-plan)
  (`merge_mode` must then be `automatic` or `manual`, and the initial trust check
  expects repository auto-merge to read as disabled).
- Add `.github/CODEOWNERS` naming the owner when `merge_mode` is `automatic`.
- Runners: the reference workflow uses `ubuntu-latest`. Self-hosted pools must
  have a runner registered for the repository before the first PR; a pool with
  one slot is covered by [waiting for verification](automatic-ci-upgrades.md#waiting-for-verification).
- Pushing files under `.github/workflows/` needs a credential with the
  `workflow` scope (an SSH remote works; a `repo`-only `gh` token is refused).
